insights: Zero comments across all 4 videos confirms call-to-actions and closing questions are currently ineffective at driving viewer replies.
Recognizable consumer brands and breakthrough hype (Tesla/SpaceX, Quantinuum) drove over 3.5x more Short views (~1,200) than NASA space exploration (335 views).
High retention did not translate to algorithmic reach: the NASA Short had 70.72% retention but only 335 views, whereas ~42-46% retention Shorts broke 1,100+ views.
Late abstract questions cause drop-off: the Quantinuum Short lost 6.1% of viewers at 42.6s during an abstract closing question about infinite dimensions.
Narrative sci-fi hooks lose viewers early: opening with 'It is 2040...' caused an 11.1% drop at 20.4s on the long-form NASA video.
Controversial debate framing drives higher engagement: the 'Real SpaceX Car Or Total Marketing Hype?' title produced 27 likes, more than double any other video.
With only 1 long-form video (23 views) and 3 Shorts, long-form and deep-dive performance data is currently too thin to draw firm conclusions.
